## 1. Why `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns` returns `-ENOENT`

`fs/kernfs/dir.c`, in `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()`:

```
	if (!parent) {
		WARN(1, KERN_WARNING "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n",
		return -ENOENT;
```
plus the earlier guard
```
	if (kernfs_type(parent) != KERNFS_DIR)
	ret = -ENOENT;
```

So the WARN fires **only when `parent` (the kernfs dir) is NULL**, i.e. the caller passed `kobj->sd == NULL`.

Caller is `fs/sysfs/symlink.c`, `sysfs_remove_link()`:
```
void sysfs_remove_link(struct kobject *kobj, const char *name)
		parent = sysfs_root_kn;
		parent = kobj->sd;
	kernfs_remove_by_name(parent, name);
```
Note there is **no `if (!parent) return;`** — `kobj->sd` is NULL once the kobject's sysfs directory has been torn down (`device_del()`), so the removal is attempted on a already-dead/never-created directory. The name being removed is `'typec'`, which pins the caller exactly.

## 2. The only creator/remover of a link literally named `"typec"`

`drivers/usb/typec/class.c` — the *only* three sites in the whole typec class that touch that name:

```
	ret = sysfs_create_link(&dev->kobj, &partner->dev.kobj, "typec");   /* typec_partner_link_device */
		sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");                    /* error unwind */
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");                            /* typec_partner_unlink_device */
```

Offending function pair:

- `static void typec_partner_link_device(struct typec_partner *partner, struct device *dev)`
- `static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner, struct device *dev)`

`dev` here is a **`struct usb_device`** (`drivers/usb/typec/class.c`: `struct usb_device *udev = to_usb_device(dev); if (udev->speed < USB_SPEED_SUPER)`), cached in the port as `port->usb2_dev` / `port->usb3_dev`.

called from `ucsi_handle_connector_change` (the `INIT_WORK(&con->work, ucsi_handle_connector_change)` workqueue item — matches `Comm: kworker/6:0`), on the disconnect branch:
```
	if (change & UCSI_CONSTAT_CONNECT_CHANGE) {

`drivers/usb/typec/class.c`, `typec_unregister_partner()`:
```
	mutex_lock(&port->partner_link_lock);
	if (port->usb2_dev) {
		typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);
		port->usb2_dev = NULL;

**It unlinks unconditionally, purely based on `port->usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` being non-NULL.** It has no record of whether a link was ever successfully created, and no check that the target device is still alive.

## 4. Root cause — two independent asymmetries

### (a) Stale `port->usb2_dev` / `usb3_dev` after the USB device is gone (primary cause)

Clearing of those pointers happens *only* in `typec_partner_deattach()`:
```
static void typec_partner_deattach(struct typec_connector *con, struct device *dev)
	if (port->usb2_dev == dev)
	else if (port->usb3_dev == dev)
		port->usb3_dev = NULL;
```
which is reachable only via `typec_deattach()` (`include/linux/usb/typec.h`), and USB core calls it from exactly one place, `drivers/usb/core/hub.c` `usb_disconnect()`:
```
		typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, &udev->dev);
```
guarded by `port_dev->connector` being non-NULL.

But `drivers/usb/core/port.c` `connector_unbind()` does:
```
	sysfs_remove_link(&connector->kobj, dev_name(dev));
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
	port_dev->connector = NULL;
```
— it **never calls `typec_deattach()` for the still-attached child**, even though the symmetric `connector_bind()` explicitly does:
```
	if (port_dev->child)
		typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);
```

Consequence: if the connector component unbinds (or the USB device is torn down on a path where `port_dev->connector` is already NULL), `port->usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` keeps a **dangling `struct device *`**. Later, when UCSI processes the disconnect and calls `typec_unregister_partner()`, `typec_partner_unlink_device()` dereferences that stale device whose `kobj->sd` is already NULL → `sysfs_remove_link()` → `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(NULL, "typec")` → the `WARN(1, "kernfs: can not remove 'typec', no directory")`. This is also a latent use-after-free, not merely a cosmetic warning.

### (b) Link creation may be skipped, but removal is not conditional

`typec_partner_link_device()` bails out early on failure (`ret = sysfs_create_link(... "typec"); if (ret) return;`), and `typec_register_partner()` only creates the links opportunistically:
```
	if (port->usb2_dev)
		typec_partner_link_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);
	if (port->usb3_dev)
		typec_partner_link_device(partner, port->usb3_dev);
```
(see also `drivers/usb/typec/class.h`: *"NOTE: These may be registered first before the typec_partner, so they will always have to be kept here instead of struct typec_partner"* — this comment is the acknowledgement of the ordering hazard).

If the `"typec"` link creation was skipped/failed (e.g. it already exists from another partner, or the udev dir is being deleted), `typec_unregister_partner()` still calls the unlink → same ENOENT WARN.

## 5. Is a fix present in this tree?

**Partially — and the relevant fix is *not* present.**

Present in this tree (a previous hardening round): `port->partner_link_lock` exists (`drivers/usb/typec/class.h`: `struct mutex partner_link_lock;`, `mutex_init(&port->partner_link_lock)` in `class.c`) and serialises `typec_register_partner` / `typec_unregister_partner` / `typec_partner_attach` / `typec_partner_deattach`. That closed the earlier *race* window, but it does **not** address either asymmetry above.

## 6. Minimal fix (matching the code as it exists here)

In `drivers/usb/core/port.c` `connector_unbind()`, mirror `connector_bind()`:
```c
	if (port_dev->child)
		typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);
	port_dev->connector = NULL;
```
and defensively in `drivers/usb/typec/class.c` `typec_partner_unlink_device()`, skip removal when the target is already unregistered (`device_is_registered(dev)` / `dev->kobj.sd`) before the two `sysfs_remove_link()` calls.
